messages.content: Answer helpfully and concisely. Retain the conversation's details.
Without tools, say READY and explain in one sentence that the Agent owns history shared by browser and terminal clients.
READY. The Agent owns a shared history that is accessible and synchronized between both the browser and terminal clients.
Without tools, continue with two sentences about how a new tab can display recent history and then live changes. Start with SHARED-HISTORY.

SHARED-HISTORY allows a new tab to initially display the recent history to provide context and continuity for the user. It then dynamically updates to reflect live changes, ensuring real-time synchronization across all clients.

In this scratch workspace, write browser-note.txt containing exactly BROWSER-CH07 plus a newline, then read it back with the file tool. Explain in about 100 words how a recorded tool result differs from a running process. Do not run any commands yet.

I will write the file browser-note.txt with the content "BROWSER-CH07\n" as requested, then read it back with the file tool.

Regarding the explanation: A recorded tool result is the captured and saved output of a tool's execution after it has completed, representing a fixed snapshot of that work. In contrast, a running process is actively executing and producing output in real time; it may also accept input and can change state asynchronously. The user can interact with or monitor a running process continuously, whereas a recorded result is static and reflects only what was produced up until the conclusion of the process.

Correction: the earlier 'without tools' restriction applied only to the first two questions and is now over. Actually invoke write_file now for browser-note.txt with content BROWSER-CH07 followed by a newline, then invoke read_file to verify it. Merely describing your intention does not complete this request.
